blockers.title: The fix for DI-B6-4 keeps deleted-but-unrecorded ids as erase = 2 and deletes them on the server again at every connection. That includes a course the owner re-imported and uploaded from another phone.
blockers.evidence: src/backup/session.ts:342-344 counts every row with a truthy `erase` (1 or 2) as an erase, so `DELETE courses id=in.(...)` runs at each settle. Lines 389-399 keep erase = 2 rows ('awaitingRecord') for as long as erased_courses is not installed, and src/persistence/serverErasures.ts:663-675 sets the value. Nothing ever retires an erase = 2 row except the migration being installed. Once it is installed, the next settle also upserts the id into erased_courses, so the course stays refused (CVERA) from then on. Decision 19 says 'Importing that course's file is your explicit choice and is accepted again'; this violates it, and it adds a new data-loss path that round 1 did not have, because b6f6715 forgot the record after the delete. Fake-backend run (installed: false): erase course X, and the record becomes {erase:2, keep:0}. Another phone puts X and its student back on the server. This phone is reopened with no user action. Output: writes ['DELETE courses <X>', 'POST rpc/app_minimum_writer_version'], then 'server courses: 0 students: 0', with the record still erase:2. The phone holding the import then loses its local copy through the download, where courseLeftThisDevice treats it as erased elsewhere and reloads. This is reachable now on the development backend, where the owner's phone checks run (B6-ERASE-RULES not yet run), and on any backend where a device erased before the migration was installed.
blockers.reproduction: Throwaway spec built on the tests/e2e/b6-erase.spec.ts helpers: withBackend(page,{installed:false}); courseWithStudent; signIn; waitUntilSent; eraseCourse; wait for erasures == [{erase:2}]; backend.table('courses').set(X, course) and the same for its student; page.reload(); wait 8 s. Expected: the re-imported course stays. Observed: it is deleted again.

importantFindings.title: Carried from DI-B6-1: a never-synced device that imported a course whose id is in erased_courses, then signs in, still loses that course without notice.
importantFindings.evidence: src/persistence/migrations.ts:498-507 treats a refused course row with reason 'erased' as 'left with the backup'. A local device that imports X records no keep (the device is not synced, src/persistence/courseArchive.ts:125). When it switches, X's course row is refused with CVERA, PowerSync reverts the rows, and courseLeftThisDevice then returns true. App.tsx reloads and prepareDatabase deletes the refusals, which held the only copy. This is the explicit import that decision 19 says is accepted again. Not run live, because the CVERA migration is not installed on the development backend.
importantFindings.reproduction: Code path; it needs the migration to run live.

qolFindings.title: Every open of an empty synced device runs a write transaction and a VACUUM.
qolFindings.evidence: migrations.ts:524-533: courseLeftThisDevice is true whenever there is no course and no non-erased course refusal, which includes a device awaiting restore and a device after an erase. Each launch then runs DELETE FROM uploadRefusals followed by compactEmptyCourseDatabase. This is harmless but repeated work at startup.

qolFindings.title: A second tab keeps showing the erased course after the erase.
qolFindings.evidence: Live two-tab run: 15 s after tab 1 erased, tab 2 still showed its heading 'D2 - 44 | 2026' (its backup state was 'checking', not connected). The erase does not broadcast to other tabs. The behaviour predates B6 and also happens on local devices.
qolFindings.reproduction: Throwaway live spec: backedUpCourse in page 1, open page 2 in the same context, erase in page 1.
